evidence: Each file's suite, the full database suites and the synthetic migration rehearsal (scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs, with Release B's live images' twelve runtime verifiers, HID_REHEARSAL_LIVE_TREE at 926b1c58) on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 clusters with fictional data only, as posted on hid-system#258 and each PR with the sha256 of each file. On the Release C integration (staging plus every lane, as merge commits): 121 of the 123 database suites pass on a superuser-owned build; my-orders and unknown-patient-record fail there exactly as on a superuser build of Release B (owner-run RLS suites a superuser bypasses) and pass, with 0147's, 0148's and 0149's own suites, on the build owned by the NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator. The Release C integration applies on a fresh Release B (0001-0146 by the runner, with Release B's runtime-grants.sql) by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator: the runner's dry run of 0147-0149 in one transaction changes nothing, the three apply, and a second run has nothing pending (services/ehr-api db:test-staging-upgrade); a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql afterwards changes no runtime privilege, so the migrations grant exactly what the file grants. On that fictional database 0147 counts 0, 0 and 0, so it creates its two roles and gives them to nobody. 0147 (Q137 B): two roles, work_list_reader (lab.work-item.read, pharmacy.work-item.read) and reading_starter (ocr.job.start), given only to the memberships 0136's own count definitions count today at real facilities through an assignment granted before 0136 was applied: work_list_reader to each administrator of 0136's lines 19 or 20 and each doctor of lines 13 or 14 (one row for a membership in both), reading_starter to each doctor of line 21; one audit row per grant in 0139's role-add form, as the system actor, with no name or account. The stop: it applies only when those counts are exactly 9, 1 and 1 (0136's dry run of 21 November) or 0, 0 and 0 (a database without those staff: the two roles are created and given to nobody, its NOTICE says so, and its post-check requires no assignment of either role and no audit row of this file). Any other counts raise 55000 with the numbers only, and nothing is applied; the suite stops it at 8/1/1, 10/1/1, 9/2/1, 9/2/2 and 9/1/0. No other role's permissions change, so Q103 A and Q111 A hold for everyone else. It replaces identity.staff_role_change_apply (SX-4's change, 0139), md5-pinned as Release B leaves it, with only lines marked 0147 (Q137 B), which the post-check strips to require Release B's md5 again: SX-4 leaves the narrow roles out of what it counts and of the role columns, refuses them as the role to add or remove, and a remove of doctor also revokes that membership's reading_starter, and its work_list_reader unless it still holds admin, each with an audit row. Locks: its table locks (NOWAIT), preconditions, count and stop are one attempt; a busy table fails the attempt and releases every lock it took, so 0147 never waits for one of its table locks while holding the others; the attempt is made 50 times, 100 ms apart (once when the transaction holds an earlier file's locks), then 55P03 with a busy refusal that starts 0147 (the runner's dry-run retry, #306), nothing applied. Any other lock wait (an index or catalog under maintenance, DDL on the replaced function, its schema, row type or language, DDL on audit.events' identity sequence, or a row the new rows' foreign key checks or triggers lock) keeps its table locks for up to the runner's lock_timeout (5 s), then stops, not retried, nothing applied (a deadlock with a staff request ends sooner, with 40P01). It holds identity.staff_facility_memberships EXCLUSIVE until commit, so an SX-4 change that starts meanwhile waits for the table and then runs D5's body (with only a row lock, a session that had run SX-4's change before ran Release B's body after 0147 committed); the cost is that it needs a moment with no staff request in flight that writes or locks a membership or inserts a row naming one (every audited staff request writes its audit row; opening a patient locks the member's own membership row), so it is run at a quiet time. No policy, grant or table changes, so it adds nothing to runtime-grants.sql. Old images on this schema: the rehearsal runs Release B's live images' runtime verifiers after 0147, and each passes. Follow-up for the owner, not part of 0147 (Rahman, #258): two of 0086's commands end the narrow roles: identity.change_facility_staff_role counts every role held, and identity.admin_set_self_service_administrator_role (S12) compares only the latest role granted other than org_admin, a narrow role after 0147; for a counted member they revoke the narrow roles with the others (S12: every role but org_admin) and grant the requested role again; access is never widened, but the same role and licence no longer answer unchanged, so S12 then makes the change, signs the member out (as every S12 grant does) and names the latest narrow role as previousRole in its audit row. 0148 (Q132 A): the pharmacy that dispensed a prescription is told when the prescriber changes it afterwards. pharmacy.prescription_changes_after_dispensing holds one row per prescription version after a work item's first dispensing (statuses before and after and SHA-256 fingerprints of the content; never the actor, the reason or a field value); append-only, row-level security on, no policy, no grant. An AFTER UPDATE trigger on ehr.prescriptions records it (it never refuses the change it follows), and pharmacy.work_item_changes_after_dispensing(uuid[]) (at most 200 ids, the session's facility, pharmacy.work-item.read and the work items' read policies as conditions) is granted to the Pharmacy runtime and the schema test runtime, as runtime-grants.sql's 0148 block grants it. Locks: ACCESS SHARE on the tables and indexes it plans on, then SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on ehr.prescriptions last, all NOWAIT within the 5 s bound; busy refusals start 0148 (the runner's dry-run retry, #306); measured on #317: the hold 15-31 ms on 20,000 rows. 0149 (ORD-7, first slice): ehr.catalog_versions, ehr.catalog_medicines, ehr.catalog_lab_tests and ehr.catalog_retired_codes (immutable rows, sealed versions, fixed ids), and ehr.search_catalog_medicines, ehr.search_catalog_lab_tests and ehr.catalog_status (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pinned) granted to the EHR runtime and the schema test runtime only, as runtime-grants.sql's 0149 block grants them; no runtime may read the tables. Nothing is loaded: the lists stay empty until the clinical lead signs a version (Q124 A) and the governed loader (#319) loads it. It locks only its own new objects, so it waits on no running service. Old images on this schema: a Release B pharmacy-api calls nothing of 0148 and a Release B ehr-api nothing of 0149; the new pharmacy-api leaves the field out and the new ehr-api answers 404/503 for the catalog on a schema without them, so either image may go first or be rolled back alone. The rehearsal runs Release B's live images' runtime verifiers after each of 0147-0149 (the runner can stop between any two files), and each passes at every point.
